recommendation: Keep the no-change audit as-is; the current build source satisfies FHIR-19962, and further edits would only restate existing scope guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-19962 was a Published FHIR-core Device change request from OO, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking that text about durable/implantable/disposable medical equipment and non-medical devices such as machines, cellphones, computers, and applications be added to the Scope and Usage introductions for both Device and DeviceDefinition.
initial_application: Commit a7f2575daae7bbacd9a22ea439c7ec35a4784f96 explicitly listed FHIR-19962 in a 2020 Device updates batch and added the requested paragraph to source/device/device-introduction.xml. That commit did not update DeviceDefinition, but related later work including FHIR-24936 in commit 578361a9000ef12bb67e86de2e5fb27ea52bd79a added equivalent DeviceDefinition scope text.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Device and DeviceDefinition as active current-build resources owned by OO. Later Device scope work, including commit 3c23148747a7d0fead21ff9afaab2fc3bb65eae9 and subsequent DeviceDefinition edits, rephrased and expanded the text while preserving the issue's substance. FHIR-18091 and FHIR-24936 are already represented on the combined branch, and community searches found no conflicting decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Device Scope and Usage currently includes the requested medical-device sentence and non-medical examples with added software/range clarification; DeviceDefinition Scope and Usage includes equivalent durable/implantable/disposable medical equipment and machine/cellphone/computer/software/application examples in its kind-of-device introduction.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Published DeviceDefinition issue used the same medical/non-medical device examples when splitting definition/comment text; it already has a combined-branch audit commit.
Published healthcare-product scope update later inserted equivalent DeviceDefinition introduction text; it already has a combined-branch audit commit.
